DECK: Discipleship Experience (Section 1) Soteriology

Q1. Why does the lesson use the example of the criminal on the cross?
A. To show that everyone receives equal earthly rewards.
B. To teach that good deeds after death determine salvation
C. To demonstrate that repentance always removes earthly consequences.
D. To illustrate that justification is a legal declaration made on the basis of Christ's substitution.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The criminal on the cross illustrates justification as a legal declaration of acquittal on the basis of Christ's substitution.
REF: Justification — 05:03–06:07; 07:06–08:16
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 8:33–34

Q2. According to the lesson, what is the strongest biblical basis for concluding that condemnation comes after a person knowingly rejects the gospel?
A. Genesis 3: 11
B. John 3:18–19
C. Romans 7: 1
D. Psalm 51: 2
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson uses John 3:18–19 to explain that condemnation applies to those who hear and understand the gospel but choose not to receive it.
REF: Original Sin — 08:41–09:41
BIBLE: Added from online research: John 3:18–19 (https://www.esv.org/verses/John%203%3A18%E2%80%9319/)

Q3. Which argument involving Jesus does Michael Heiser use to challenge the view that every person inherits Adam's personal guilt?
A. Jesus obeyed the Law perfectly.
B. If everyone born through Adam is automatically guilty, Jesus would also have been guilty.
C. Jesus' miracles prove He was sinless.
D. Jesus never discussed original sin.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Michael Heiser's argument is that if everyone born through Adam automatically inherited personal guilt, then Jesus would also be guilty.
REF: Original Sin — 03:22–04:13
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 5:12 | Added from online research: Hebrews 4:15 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Hebrews%2B4%3A15/)

Q4. In the salvation lesson, why are both Nicodemus and Cornelius discussed?
A. To demonstrate that both moral and religious people still needed salvation through faith in Christ.
B. To compare Jewish and Roman cultures.
C. To explain the history of evangelism.
D. To illustrate different spiritual gifts.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: Nicodemus and Cornelius illustrate that moral or religious standing does not replace the need to receive the gospel and be saved through faith in Christ.
REF: Born Again — 06:39–08:30
BIBLE: Added from online research: John 3:1–10 (https://www.esv.org/verses/John+3%3A1%E2%80%9310/); Acts 10:34–48 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Acts+10%3A34%E2%80%9348/)

Q5. Which statement best summarizes the lesson's definition of being born again?
A. Becoming more disciplined in religious practice.
B. Joining a local church.
C. Living a morally upright life.
D. Receiving the life of God through faith in Christ.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: Being born again is receiving God's supernatural life through faith in Jesus, rather than earning it by behavior.
REF: Born Again — 08:30–10:04
BIBLE: Added from online research: John 3:3–8 (https://www.esv.org/verses/John%2B3%3A3%E2%80%938/)

Q6. According to the lesson on righteousness, believers are described as "accepted in the Beloved" because:
A. They consistently obey God's commands.
B. They no longer require repentance.
C. Christ's work secures their acceptance before God.
D. They possess greater spiritual gifts than others.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: Believers are accepted in the Beloved because Christ took their place and secured the benefits of His work.
REF: Righteousness — 04:26–05:11
BIBLE: Added from online research: Ephesians 1:6 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Ephesians%2B1%3A6/)

Q7. Which statement best reflects the lesson's explanation of right standing with God?
A. It depends on maintaining perfect obedience.
B. It depends on sincere intentions.
C. It is grounded in faith in Christ rather than personal behaviour.
D. It is earned through consistent repentance.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson says right standing with God rests on faith in Christ and what He has done, not on how well a person behaves.
REF: Righteousness — 06:12–06:53
BIBLE: Added from online research: Romans 3:22–24 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Romans%2B3%3A22%E2%80%9324/)

Q8. Why does the lesson distinguish between metamelomai and metanoia?
A. To argue that sorrow alone is insufficient because it should lead to repentance.
B. To show they can be used similarly.
C. To teach that repentance belongs only to the Old Testament.
D. To show the role of emotions in repentance.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The distinction shows that sorrow is not itself repentance; the lesson says godly sorrow leads to repentance.
REF: Repentance — 04:41–05:47
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 2 Corinthians 7

Q9. What role does the pornography illustration serve in the lesson?
A. To explain discipline and it's role in a believer.
B. To show that behavioural change alone is not the same as gospel repentance.
C. To teach that addiction can be overcome just by making changes.
D. To argue against moral discipline.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The example shows that stopping an outward behavior alone is not gospel repentance; repentance turns toward Christ.
REF: Repentance — 01:54–02:46
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Mark 1:15

Q10. Why does the lesson distinguish redemption from justification?
A. Redemption describes Christ's saving work, while justification describes God's legal declaration concerning the believer.
B. Redemption applies to Old Testament, while justification applies to the Church now.
C. Redemption concerns forgiveness, while justification concerns rewards.
D. They are presented as completely unrelated doctrines.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: Redemption describes Christ's saving provision through His death and resurrection, while justification is the legal declaration that the believer is not guilty.
REF: Justification — 09:24–10:31

Q11. Apostle's final position on original sin is that humanity inherits:
A. Adam's guilt alone.
B. Mortality together with an irresistible tendency to sin.
C. Physical death without any inclination toward sin.
D. Immediate spiritual condemnation at birth.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says humanity receives mortality from Adam and describes an irresistible tendency for the natural person to sin.
REF: Original Sin — 02:19–03:22; 10:47–11:43
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 5:12; Romans 7; Romans 8

Q12. Which statement best reflects the lesson's teaching about the moment a person is saved?
A. At water baptism.
B. At the altar call.
C. At the point of genuine faith in Christ.
D. After completing discipleship classes.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker says a person receives Christ's life and is saved at the point of placing genuine faith in Jesus.
REF: Born Again — 10:04–11:39
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: John 3:16; Acts 10:43

Q13. According to the lesson, why does Paul repeatedly affirm believers' identity before correcting their conduct?
A. Because identity provides the foundation from which lasting transformation occurs.
B. Because behaviour is unimportant.
C. Because discipline belongs only to church leaders.
D. Because sin disappears after conversion.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: Paul emphasizes believers' identity in Christ by grace as a basis for realigning their conduct.
REF: Righteousness — 01:48–03:34
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 1 Corinthians 1:4; 1 Corinthians 5; 1 Corinthians 6; 1 Corinthians 14; 1 Corinthians 11

Q14. What is the significance of Luke 24:47 in the repentance lesson?
A. It limits repentance to the nation of Israel.
B. It shows repentance and forgiveness are to be proclaimed to all nations.
C. It teaches repentance is unnecessary after Christ's resurrection.
D. It defines repentance as sorrow alone.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson cites Luke 24:47 to show that repentance and remission of sins should be preached to all nations.
REF: Repentance — 10:09–11:08
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Luke 24:47 | Also cited in lesson segment: Acts 2; Acts 11:18

Q15. The lesson explains that once God declares a believer justified:
A. Other accusations remain equally authoritative.
B. The believer must continually earn that verdict.
C. No other opinion overrides God's verdict.
D. The believer no longer faces any earthly consequences.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: Once the judge declares someone not guilty, the lesson says no other opinion overrides that verdict.
REF: Justification — 07:06–08:16
BIBLE: Added from online research: Romans 8:33–34 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Romans+8%3A33%E2%80%9334/)

Q16. Which statement best integrates the teaching across the salvation and righteousness lessons?
A. Spiritual life begins through faith in Christ, and that new identity becomes the basis for transformed living.
B. Spiritual growth must precede salvation.
C. Good behaviour produces spiritual life.
D. Identity in Christ replaces the need for obedience.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The salvation lesson says faith in Jesus brings Christ's life; the righteousness lesson says identity in Christ by grace influences behavior.
REF: Born Again — 09:15–10:04; Righteousness — 01:48–03:34
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: John 3:16; 1 Corinthians 1:4; Ephesians 1:3

Q17. Across the week's lessons, which recurring pattern best describes how God transforms people?
A. Behaviour changes first, then God grants acceptance.
B. God grants acceptance in Christ, and that reality shapes a transformed life.
C. Fear of judgment produces lasting holiness.
D. Religious discipline creates spiritual life.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents acceptance in Christ by grace as the foundation for realigning believers' conduct.
REF: Righteousness — 01:48–03:34; 04:26–05:11
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 1 Corinthians 1:4; 1 Corinthians 5; 1 Corinthians 6; 1 Corinthians 14; 1 Corinthians 11; Ephesians 1:3

Q18. Which statement best captures the relationship between faith and repentance as presented throughout the lessons?
A. Faith removes any expectation of changed living.
B. Repentance earns salvation before faith.
C. Faith in Christ brings salvation, while genuine repentance accompanies that faith and produces its fruit.
D. Repentance and faith are unrelated ideas.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lessons connect salvation with faith in Jesus and describe genuine repentance as turning toward Christ, with behavior change as its fruit.
REF: Born Again — 10:04–10:54; Repentance — 06:53–08:04; 13:36–14:40
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: John 3:16; Romans 10; Matthew 3:8; Luke 3; Acts 26:20

Q19. Looking across all five lessons, which statement most accurately summarizes the central message?
A. Christianity is primarily about becoming morally disciplined.
B. Salvation is God's gracious work in Christ, received through faith, resulting in a new identity that produces transformed living.
C. The Christian life is sustained mainly through religious activities.
D. The gospel is chiefly a call to improve personal behaviour.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Across the lessons, salvation is presented as God's work in Christ received through faith, with acceptance in Christ leading to transformed conduct.
REF: Born Again — 08:30–10:54; Original Sin — 08:41–09:41; Repentance — 06:53–08:04; 13:36–14:40; Justification — 05:03–06:07; 09:24–10:31; Righteousness — 01:48–03:34; 05:11–06:53
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: John 3:16; Romans 8:1; 1 Corinthians 1:4; Acts 26:20

Q20. Which statement best explains why the lesson begins by discussing God's role as Judge before defining justification?
A. To establish that justification should be understood as a legal declaration rather than merely a feeling of forgiveness.
B. To show that believers should fear God's judgment every day.
C. To demonstrate that Old Testament believers understood salvation exactly as Christians do today.
D. To explain why every Christian will receive earthly rewards.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The introduction establishes the legal setting by identifying God as Judge and describing justification and condemnation in legal terms.
REF: Justification — 01:16–04:06
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Genesis 18:25; 1 Samuel 2:10; Psalm 7:11; Romans 14:10, 12; 2 Corinthians 5:10; Romans 8

Q21. In the lesson on original sin, what distinction is presented as central to interpreting Romans 5:12?
A. Humanity inherited Adam's personal guilt.
B. Humanity inherited death and an eventual tendency to sin rather than Adam's personal guilt.
C. Humanity inherited neither death nor sin from Adam.
D. Humanity only inherited physical weakness from Adam.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker distinguishes mortality received from Adam from Adam's personal guilt, then describes an irresistible tendency to sin.
REF: Original Sin — 02:19–03:22; 10:47–11:43
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Romans 5:12 | Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 7; Romans 8

Q22. The CNDP framework introduced in the salvation lesson is primarily intended to help believers:
A. Memorize the order of the New Testament books.
B. Explain salvation in a complete and coherent way.
C. Compare different theological traditions.
D. Study biblical Greek more effectively.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: CNDP organizes the lesson around the context, necessity, definition, and provision of salvation.
REF: Born Again — 02:06–03:06

Q23. Paul's approach to correcting the Corinthians' moral failures was to:
A. First question whether they were truly saved.
B. Focus primarily on punishment as motivation for holiness.
C. Emphasize their identity in Christ before addressing their conduct.
D. Remove members involved in every form of sin before teaching them.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: Paul emphasizes the Corinthians' identity in Christ by grace and uses it as a basis to realign their conduct.
REF: Righteousness — 01:48–03:34
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 1 Corinthians 1:4; 1 Corinthians 5; 1 Corinthians 6; 1 Corinthians 14; 1 Corinthians 11

Q24. Which statement best captures the lesson's understanding of genuine repentance?
A. It is turning to Christ in faith, producing an inner change that naturally bears fruit in conduct.
B. It is behavioural reform that earns God's acceptance.
C. It is simply feeling remorse for past actions.
D. It is abandoning sinful habits before believing the gospel.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: Repentance is turning toward Christ with an inner resolve that eventually bears fruit in conduct.
REF: Repentance — 06:53–08:04; 13:36–14:40
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 10; Matthew 3:8; Luke 3; Acts 26:20

Q25. The courtroom illustration used in the justification lesson primarily emphasizes that:
A. Every believer will eventually stand trial again.
B. Justification changes a person's legal standing before God because of Christ's substitution.
C. Christians must defend themselves before God.
D. Good works overturn past guilt.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The courtroom illustration presents justification as a legal verdict of acquittal on the basis of Christ's substitution.
REF: Justification — 05:03–06:07; 07:06–08:16
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 8:33–34

Q26. Why does Apostle disagree, at least in part, with Michael Heiser's final conclusion?
A. He believes Adam's guilt alone explains human sinfulness.
B. He believes children should be considered guilty from birth.
C. He believes Romans 5 should not be used when discussing original sin.
D. He believes mortality alone cannot explain why every human eventually sins.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker disagrees in part because mortality alone does not explain why humans eventually sin; he also argues for an irresistible tendency to sin.
REF: Original Sin — 10:47–11:43

Q27. Which illustration is used to explain that a person may appear physically alive while lacking spiritual life?
A. A courtroom verdict
B. A ledger balancing debts
C. A funeral where the body looked unchanged
D. A child learning to walk
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The funeral story illustrates that a body may appear unchanged after life has departed, introducing the lesson's explanation of spiritual life.
REF: Born Again — 04:46–05:40

Q28. According to the lesson on righteousness, why does Paul remind believers that their bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit?
A. To convince them they have permanently lost God's presence.
B. To use their identity in Christ as the basis for transformed behaviour.
C. To teach that holiness depends on human effort.
D. To discourage participation in public worship.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Paul reminds believers that their bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit and uses their identity and relationship with God to encourage changed behavior.
REF: Righteousness — 02:47–03:34
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 1 Corinthians 6:19

Q29. Why does the lesson distinguish between repentance and its fruit?
A. Because repentance is an inward turning to God that should eventually produce outward obedience.
B. Because behavioural change has no place in the Christian life.
C. Because repentance only applies before salvation.
D. Because obedience and repentance always mean the same thing.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson distinguishes repentance from its fruit by describing repentance as an inward turning to God, while changed behavior is its fruit.
REF: Repentance — 13:36–14:40
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 10; Matthew 3:8; Luke 3; Acts 26:20

Q30. The Greek word dikaio, as explained in the lesson, most accurately means to:
A. Become morally perfect over time.
B. Be declared righteous or acquitted.
C. Earn righteousness through obedience.
D. Receive power for holy living.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson defines the term as to declare righteous, acquit, or vindicate.
REF: Justification — 05:03–06:07

Q31. What does the speaker say the term "soteriology" refers to?
A. The study of human sin and its effects on the soul
B. The study of salvation, from the Greek soteria and logi
C. The study of final judgment and the end of the age
D. The study of the church and how it carries out its mission
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker opens the series by explaining that soteria is the Greek word for salvation and logi means study, so soteriology is the study of salvation.
REF: ORIGINAL SIN — [00:16]

Q32. How did some people interpret Romans 5:14, which says death reigned even over those who had not sinned in the way Adam did?
A. As showing that death comes only to those who personally commit sin as Adam did
B. As showing that Adam's sin affected only the first generation after the fall
C. As showing that infants are spared death until they reach an age to choose
D. As showing that Adam's guilt has passed to every person, even before sin
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker says the idea of death passing to those who had not sinned like Adam led people to conclude that Adam's guilt was passed on to all, so a person is born a sinner before sinning.
REF: ORIGINAL SIN — [01:14]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Romans 5:14 | Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 5:12

Q33. On the view that Adam's guilt is passed on to everyone at birth, what does the speaker say follows for infants and for people unable to hear and believe the gospel?
A. They would be counted as sinners and go where sinners go
B. They would be saved automatically because they cannot understand the gospel
C. They would be held in a separate category until they are old enough to choose
D. They would be judged only by the sins their parents committed
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says that on this understanding the answer is yes: infants who die are sinners who go where sinners go, and mentally challenged people who cannot hear and believe the gospel go to hell. He then challenges this view.
REF: ORIGINAL SIN — [01:14; 02:19]

Q34. According to the scholars the speaker cites, what does Romans 5:12 actually say spread to all men?
A. Sin along with Adam's guilt
B. A fully formed sinful nature
C. Death, rather than sin itself
D. Condemnation for every newborn
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: Scholars note that in Romans 5:12 it is death that passed to all men, not sin; the speaker repeats that death spread to all men because all have sinned.
REF: ORIGINAL SIN — [02:19; 03:22]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Romans 5:12

Q35. How does the speaker describe the view that humanity received no consequence at all from Adam's sin?
A. As the view that best fits Romans 5:14 on its own terms
B. As a sound middle ground between the two positions he describes
C. As a view he accepts for infants but not for adults
D. As the opposite extreme, which he calls a theological heresy
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: After describing the guilt view, the speaker says some go to the other extreme, a theological heresy that denies any consequence of Adam's sin; what is actually received is death and a propensity to eventually sin.
REF: ORIGINAL SIN — [02:19]

Q36. How does Michael Heiser, as the speaker reports it, respond to the claim that the virgin birth shields Jesus from inherited sin?
A. He asks why sin would pass only through the father when Mary also contributed biologically
B. He argues that the virgin birth is not clearly recorded in the Gospel accounts of Jesus' birth
C. He argues that Joseph's seed was needed for Jesus to fully share in human nature
D. He argues that Jesus avoided sin because Mary was herself sinless from birth
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker recounts that Heiser asked who says sin is transmitted only through the man, since a woman carried Jesus and he shares a woman's attributes, which undermines the virgin-birth defense.
REF: ORIGINAL SIN — [04:13]

Q37. What problem does Michael Heiser raise for the view that everyone born through Adam's lineage is a sinner?
A. It would mean Jesus never faced temptation.
B. It would mean Jesus, even if he never committed sin, would also be a sinner.
C. It would mean Adam was never guilty.
D. It would mean Romans 5 is not Scripture.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Heiser argues that if birth through Adam's lineage alone makes someone a sinner, Jesus would be a sinner too.
REF: Original Sin — 03:22–04:13
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 5:12 | Added from online research: Hebrews 4:15 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Hebrews%2B4%3A15/)

Q38. What does the speaker give as the simple answer for why Jesus did not commit sin?
A. Because he was born of a virgin
B. Because Jesus is God himself
C. Because Mary was sinless
D. Because he kept the Law
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says the simple answer is that Jesus is God. He adds that the Bible does not categorically say the virgin birth is the reason, and that the claim that Mary was sinless is not biblical.
REF: ORIGINAL SIN — [05:14]
BIBLE: Added from online research: John 1:1 (https://www.esv.org/verses/John+1%3A1/); Hebrews 4:15 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Hebrews+4%3A15/)

Q39. What point does the speaker attribute to William Lane Craig about Jesus' use of children as illustrations of the kingdom?
A. Children illustrate the kingdom only as a picture of humility, with no deeper meaning
B. Jesus used children to teach that guilt is inherited but can be set aside by humility
C. Jesus would not have used them as he did if he thought they carried Adam's guilt
D. Jesus used children to show that infants must be baptized before entering the kingdom
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker reports Craig's argument, citing Mark 10:14 and Matthew 18:3-6, that Jesus placed a premium on little ones and would not set them forth as models for entering the kingdom if they carried Adam's guilt.
REF: ORIGINAL SIN — [06:03; 06:56; 07:46]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Mark 10:14; Matthew 18:3–6

Q40. How does the speaker describe the "age of accountability"?
A. The age at which someone can hear the gospel, understand it, and accept or reject it
B. The age at which a person is first held responsible for the sin Adam committed
C. The age at which a person is first able to sin and is therefore called a sinner
D. The age at which a person becomes eligible for baptism and church membership
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: Reading John 3:18-19, the speaker says condemnation falls on those who hear and understand the gospel but choose not to receive it, which requires reaching what theologians call the age of accountability.
REF: ORIGINAL SIN — [08:41]
BIBLE: Added from online research: John 3:18–19 (https://www.esv.org/verses/John%203%3A18%E2%80%9319/)

Q41. What does the speaker say Michael Heiser claims about Augustine's explanation of original sin?
A. Augustine rejected Romans 5:12 as unreliable and built his view mainly on the Gospel of John
B. Augustine read the original Greek carefully and found Adam's guilt clearly taught there
C. Augustine taught only that death, and never guilt, was passed on from Adam to his children
D. Augustine used a Latin translation that mistranslated a word, which led to the guilt view
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker reports Heiser's claim that Augustine, a Latin speaker, worked from a Latin translation that mistranslated a particular word, which led to several centuries of the view that guilt passed on.
REF: ORIGINAL SIN — [09:41]

Q42. What does the speaker say about when a person becomes a sinner, given that all people will eventually sin?
A. They are sinners from conception, though their guilt is counted only later
B. They become sinners when they first hear and reject the gospel
C. They are not sinners until they themselves actually commit sin
D. They become sinners at the moment they are born into Adam's line
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker says that even though all men will eventually sin, they are not sinners until they do.
REF: ORIGINAL SIN — [10:47]

Q43. How does the speaker himself define original sin?
A. Adam's personal guilt, which makes every person a sinner from the moment of birth
B. An irresistible tendency to sin that means every man, though born innocent, will eventually sin
C. Mortality inherited from Adam, with no real tendency toward sin attached to it at any stage of life
D. A spiritual condition that makes it impossible for infants who die to be saved
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says mortality from Adam is not enough to explain why everyone sins (he points to Romans 7 and 8) and defines original sin as an irresistible tendency in the natural man to sin, though born innocent.
REF: ORIGINAL SIN — [10:47]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Romans 7 | Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 5; Romans 8

Q44. How does the speaker say people who cannot receive or understand the gospel, such as infants, are judged?
A. By the same standard that applies to everyone who has been born into Adam's line of descent
B. By the response their parents gave when they heard the gospel
C. By whether they were dedicated to God or baptized as young children
D. By a different metric from those able to hear, receive, or reject the gospel
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker says that as long as someone is not in a position to hear, receive, or reject the gospel, God has a different rule for them; people in infancy or other states where they cannot understand it are judged by a different metric.
REF: ORIGINAL SIN — [09:41; 11:43]

Q45. What do the four letters of the speaker's CNDP framework stand for?
A. Conviction, New birth, Discipline, Prayer
B. Calling, Newness, Devotion, Perseverance
C. Context, Necessity, Definition, Provision
D. Christ, Need, Discipleship, Promise
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker says CNDP is not even an acronym, just key letters to remember: C for context, N for necessity, D for definition, and P for provision.
REF: BORN AGAIN — [02:06]

Q46. What does the speaker draw from Jesus' contrast between being born of the flesh and born of the Spirit in John 3?
A. Just as biological life has an origin, spiritual life in Christ must have a beginning
B. Spiritual life is simply a continuation of biological life, sustained by religious practice
C. Spiritual birth happens gradually as a person matures in good behavior over time
D. Physical birth is sinful, while spiritual birth is a holy event given to the faithful
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says there is an origin to biological life and Jesus is saying there must be an origin to spiritual life in Christ: life in Christ will have no end, but it will have a beginning.
REF: BORN AGAIN — [03:06; 03:55]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: John 3 | Also cited in lesson segment: Genesis 3; Ephesians 2

Q47. When Adam ate the fruit, the speaker says he was "still walking, still talking, but he was dead." What is his point?
A. God's warning about death was postponed until the time of Adam's physical death
B. The spiritual part of man died in Genesis 3 even though Adam stayed physically alive
C. Adam's body began dying right away, while his spirit stayed fully alive in God
D. Adam lost his ability to hear God clearly but kept his spiritual life intact
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says something fundamentally wrong happened in Genesis 3 when the spiritual part of man died, which is why God said Adam would surely die; Ephesians 2 then speaks of believers dead in trespasses and sins who were made alive.
REF: BORN AGAIN — [03:55; 04:46]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Genesis 3; Ephesians 2

Q48. What does the speaker conclude from the first burial he attended as a young boy?
A. Kind and generous people do not truly die.
B. A dead person can be revived by good behaviour.
C. The body is just a casing, and something inside the man was missing even though he looked the same.
D. Burials are the best setting in which to preach salvation.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The man looked much the same in the coffin, but something inside him was missing. The speaker realised the body is just a casing and that spiritual life can be imparted.
REF: Born Again — 04:46–05:40

Q49. Which part of a person is born again, according to the lesson, and how far does its effect reach?
A. The body, with no effect on the soul or spirit
B. The soul, with no effect on the spirit or body
C. The spirit, with its efficacy extending to the soul and eventually the body
D. The mind, with its effect limited to what a person believes
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The spiritual part is what is born again, though its efficacy goes beyond the spirit to the soul and eventually the body.
REF: Born Again — 05:40
BIBLE: Added from online research: John 3:5–6 (https://www.esv.org/verses/John+3%3A5%E2%80%936/)

Q50. Why does the speaker contrast a rowdy "gangster" type with a calm, successful, non-religious person?
A. Wealthy, successful people are harder to reach with the gospel than anyone else, because they feel no need
B. Visible vices, rather than unbelief, are what bring a person under condemnation
C. Rowdy people are more open to the gospel than people who are morally upright
D. We feel less urgency for well-behaved unbelievers, though they also need faith in Jesus
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker says we are moved with compassion for people with visible vices, but feel less incentive to see the futility of a well-behaved person's efforts if he does not place faith in Jesus; Jesus told even a morally excellent Nicodemus he must be born again.
REF: BORN AGAIN — [05:40; 06:39]
BIBLE: Added from online research: John 3:1–10 (https://www.esv.org/verses/John+3%3A1%E2%80%9310/); Acts 10:34–48 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Acts+10%3A34%E2%80%9348/)

Q51. What does the lesson conclude from Jesus telling the morally excellent Nicodemus "you must be born again" and from Cornelius having to send for Peter?
A. Salvation is reserved for people of high moral excellence.
B. Religious leaders must be saved before ordinary people.
C. Attending church is enough for those who behave well.
D. Salvation is not about good behaviour but about faith in Jesus.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: Both men were well behaved yet needed salvation. The speaker adds that being in a garage does not make you a car, so going to church does not make you born again.
REF: Born Again — 07:36
BIBLE: Added from online research: John 3:1–10 (https://www.esv.org/verses/John+3%3A1%E2%80%9310/); Acts 10:34–48 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Acts+10%3A34%E2%80%9348/)

Q52. Which other biblical term does the lesson give for being born again, described as a translation from the kingdom of darkness into the kingdom of light?
A. Consecration
B. Redemption
C. Repentance
D. Regeneration
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker says the Bible also calls being born again regeneration.
REF: Born Again — 08:30
BIBLE: Added from online research: Titus 3:5 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Titus+3%3A5/); Colossians 1:13 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Colossians+1%3A13/)

Q53. What does the lesson say the transfer from darkness into light requires, and how does it support this with Paul?
A. Behaviour; Paul says the gospel is a standard believers must keep.
B. Knowledge; Paul says the gospel is wisdom reserved for the learned.
C. Power, not behaviour; Paul says he is not ashamed of the gospel because it is the power of God unto salvation to those who believe.
D. Discipline; Paul says the gospel rewards those who are faithful.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker says this transfer takes power, not behaviour, and cites Paul on the gospel as the power of God unto salvation.
REF: Born Again — 08:30
BIBLE: Added from online research: Romans 1:16 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Romans+1%3A16/); Colossians 1:13 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Colossians+1%3A13/)

Q54. Why does the speaker quote "If the Lord should count iniquities, who shall stand?" when introducing provision?
A. To show that no one can meet the requirements for salvation by works, so God's provision is needed
B. To teach believers to fear judgment every day
C. To show that sin is less serious for religious people
D. To show that confession must come before faith
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says none of us can meet the requirements for salvation by works. John 3:16 is then presented as God's provision.
REF: Born Again — 09:15–10:04
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: John 3:16 | Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 9

Q55. The lesson presents John 3:16 as God's provision. What does it say a person must specifically place faith in, and how does it describe the roles of the heart and the mouth?
A. That Jesus died for his sins and rose again for his justification; with the heart man believes unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation
B. That Jesus was a great moral teacher; the mouth alone saves and belief in the heart is optional
C. That Jesus will reward good behaviour; belief in the heart saves and confession is unnecessary
D. That God overlooks the sins of religious people; the heart produces good works and the mouth produces righteousness
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: Faith is placed in Jesus who died for our sins and rose for our justification. The speaker cites the verse that heart belief is unto righteousness and mouth confession is unto salvation.
REF: Born Again — 10:04–10:54
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: John 3:16 | Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 10:9–10

Q56. What does the speaker say the Acts 10 account of Cornelius's household shows about when people receive the Holy Spirit and are saved?
A. The Spirit came only after Peter finished his sermon and gave an invitation to receive
B. The Spirit fell while Peter was still speaking, when they placed their faith in Jesus
C. The Spirit came only after the household was baptized in water as Peter instructed
D. The Spirit came only after they had proved their devotion to God over a period of time
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker cites Acts 10: while Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit fell on all who heard, because faith was in their hearts before he even reached the point of an invitation.
REF: BORN AGAIN — [11:39]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Acts 10

Q57. How does the speaker describe the relationship between receiving Christ's life and giving one's life to Christ?
A. Receiving Christ's life comes first; consecration follows because the life lived is his
B. Giving one's life to Christ comes first, and he then responds by granting new life
C. Both happen only after a believer completes a period of formal discipleship training
D. They are one and the same act, so they cannot be meaningfully told apart
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says salvation is receiving the life of Christ and the Holy Spirit; only then can a person give his life in consecration and service, because the life he now lives is Christ's (Galatians 2:20).
REF: BORN AGAIN — [12:24]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Galatians 2:20

Q58. If someone says, "I'm a good person and I even behave better than many people in your church," what does the speaker want a believer to be able to do?
A. Agree that good behavior is enough to please God and invite the person to attend church
B. Compare the person's behavior with that of church members to settle who is better
C. Explain that being born again is receiving Christ's life by faith, not being well behaved
D. Wait until the person has felt enough guilt about sin before speaking about Christ at all
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker says a believer must be able to articulate that, as biological life has an origin, being born again means placing faith in Jesus and receiving the life of Christ and the Holy Spirit, rather than being well behaved.
REF: BORN AGAIN — [09:15]
BIBLE: Added from online research: John 3:3 (https://www.esv.org/verses/John+3%3A3/); Ephesians 2:8–10 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Ephesians+2%3A8%E2%80%9310/)

Q59. What problem does the speaker identify in preaching that treats behavioral modification as the finality of repentance?
A. It overemphasizes forgiveness while ignoring the place of guilt over past sins entirely
B. It treats a mere change of mind as sufficient and denies any place for outward change
C. It teaches that repentance was meant only for the Jews who had rejected Christ
D. It says almost nothing about what Christ did and mainly aims to make people feel guilty
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker says some preachers slip works-consciousness into salvation by making behavioral modification the finality of repentance, with almost no mention of what Christ did and a goal of making people feel guilty about their past.
REF: REPENTANCE — [00:16; 00:55]
BIBLE: Added from online research: Titus 3:5 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Titus+3%3A5/)

Q60. According to the speaker's reading of Mark 1:15, what makes repentance gospel-centered?
A. How deep a person's sorrow about their past sins happens to be
B. Who a person turns to, not merely what they turn away from
C. How completely a person abandons one particular sinful habit
D. How publicly a person announces the decision to change
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Citing Mark 1:15 (repent and believe in the gospel), the speaker says repentance is turning away from something, but what makes it gospel-centric is what, and more specifically who, a person turns to.
REF: REPENTANCE — [02:46]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Mark 1:15

Q61. What careful claim does the speaker make against those who say repentance is only a change of mind with no behavioral modification?
A. Behavioral change is not required for salvation but is a necessary fruit of genuine salvation
B. Behavioral change is required for salvation alongside faith, since faith alone is incomplete
C. Behavioral change is optional for believers and matters mainly for church leaders
D. A change of mind comes only after the person's behavior has already changed first
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says he is choosing his words carefully: he is not saying behavioral change is required for salvation, but that it is a necessary fruit of genuine salvation.
REF: REPENTANCE — [03:39]
BIBLE: Added from online research: Matthew 3:8 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Matt.%203%3A8/); Acts 26:20 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Acts%2B26%3A20/)

Q62. What does the speaker say people who use 2 Corinthians 7 to separate metamelomai from metanoia overlook?
A. Paul used the two Greek words as exact synonyms throughout the passage
B. Paul never mentions sorrow anywhere in the passage
C. Paul himself said that godly sorrow leads to repentance
D. Paul taught that sorrow itself is what saves a person
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: In 2 Corinthians 7 the contrast is between being made sorry (metamelomai) and repentance (metanoia), but the speaker notes Paul said godly sorrow leads to repentance, even though feeling bad is not what saves; the blood of Jesus saves.
REF: REPENTANCE — [04:41; 05:47]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: 2 Corinthians 7

Q63. In the speaker's view, what saves a person in relation to a change of lifestyle?
A. The lifestyle change itself, provided that it is sincere and lasting over time
B. The faith that made the person turn away, not the lifestyle change itself
C. Faith alone, with no need for any resolve to turn away from sin
D. A feeling of sorrow that is deep enough to produce a real change
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says it is not the change of lifestyle but the faith that made you turn away that saves, yet that faith is not genuine without a genuine resolve to turn away from those things.
REF: REPENTANCE — [08:04]
BIBLE: Added from online research: Ephesians 2:8–10 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Ephesians+2%3A8%E2%80%9310/); Mark 1:15 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Mark+1%3A15/)

Q64. How does the speaker respond to the claim that preaching "just believe in Jesus" is enough?
A. It is incorrect because it leaves out repentance and so misleads those who hear it
B. It is complete as it stands and needs no further qualification from other texts
C. It is correct only when preached to Gentiles, for whom repentance is not required
D. It is not wrong, just incomplete, because real faith includes a resolve to turn from sin
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker says that telling people to just believe in Jesus is not incorrect, just incomplete, and he warns of a thin line between grace and lasciviousness.
REF: REPENTANCE — [08:04]
BIBLE: Added from online research: Mark 1:15 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Mark+1%3A15/)

Q65. What does the speaker's example of resolving never again to give money to an ungrateful person show about repentance?
A. Repentance is not work but an internal posture change that will influence behavior
B. Repentance is the first outward act of refusal, which others can observe and verify
C. Repentance must first be proven through works before it can count as genuine
D. Repentance depends mainly on how badly other people have treated you in the past
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says the resolve is not yet works but a changed internal posture that influences future behavior, and that repentance is likewise not work but a posture change that will influence works.
REF: REPENTANCE — [09:04]
BIBLE: Added from online research: 2 Corinthians 7:10–11 (https://www.esv.org/verses/2+Corinthians+7%3A10%E2%80%9311/)

Q66. What does the speaker conclude from Acts 11:18, where the Gentiles are granted "repentance to life"?
A. Repentance was offered to the Gentiles only after they had first changed their behavior
B. Repentance is mainly remorse over having been part of the crucifixion of Christ
C. Repentance is a change of mind focused on eternal life, which if genuine will affect lifestyle
D. Repentance to life is meant only for Jews who had earlier rejected Christ
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker says Acts 11:18 shows repentance for Gentiles is a change of mind focused on receiving eternal life, not first of all a change of behavior, though a genuine change of mind will influence a change of lifestyle.
REF: REPENTANCE — [11:08]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Acts 11:18 | Also cited in lesson segment: Acts 2; Luke 24:47

Q67. How does the speaker interpret confessing "the Lord Jesus" in Romans 10:9?
A. It means repeating a confession that secures salvation regardless of one's lifestyle
B. It means receiving his lordship and living by his commands in response to his grace
C. It means earning one's salvation by faithfully obeying his commands each day
D. It means keeping one's salvation intact by avoiding sin and its consequences
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says confessing Jesus as Lord means receiving his lordship and living by his commands; faith brings responsibilities, not in order to keep salvation but in response to what he has freely done.
REF: REPENTANCE — [12:15]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Romans 10:9 | Also cited in lesson segment: Acts 11:18

Q68. How does the speaker respond to the extreme that treats obedience as synonymous with repentance?
A. Repentance consists of the works that show that a person has turned from sin
B. Works consistent with repentance are optional for those who genuinely believe
C. Repentance and behavior change have no necessary connection to each other at all
D. Repentance is an inner resolve to serve the Lord, and behavior change is only its fruit
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: Citing Matthew 3:8 and Acts 26:20, the speaker says repentance is a posture change, an inner resolve to serve the Lord, and that the behavior change is the fruit of repentance, not repentance in itself.
REF: REPENTANCE — [13:36]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Matthew 3:8; Acts 26:20 | Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 10; Luke 3

Q69. According to the speaker, does a believer's ongoing struggle with sin show that their salvation is not genuine?
A. No; like a baby learning to walk, a genuine believer can struggle yet resolve to turn
B. Yes; any continued struggle with sin shows that the repentance was never genuine
C. Yes, unless the struggle ends within a short time after the person first believes
D. No, because ongoing struggle has no connection to whether someone has repented
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says a person who genuinely believes and repents may still be struggling like a baby learning to walk, and that does not invalidate his salvation; he points to Jesus' teaching on forgiving seven times a day.
REF: REPENTANCE — [14:40]

Q70. What does the speaker say is one way to show you are truly saved and have divine life in you?
A. A complete absence of any struggle with the sins of one's former life
B. A strong sense of guilt that never lifts, however much one has repented
C. A sensitivity to sin that breaks your heart and prompts a resolve to turn
D. A visible record of moral reform that others can point to and confirm
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker says one sign of real divine life is a sensitivity to sin: it breaks your heart that you, having received so much love, would still indulge in it, and there should be a resolve to turn away because you are free in Christ.
REF: REPENTANCE — [15:41]
BIBLE: Added from online research: 2 Corinthians 7:10–11 (https://www.esv.org/verses/2+Corinthians+7%3A10%E2%80%9311/)

Q71. What image does the speaker use for the right knowledge of God, and which two extremes does it warn against?
A. A razor blade, risking a fall into lasciviousness or works consciousness
B. A narrow bridge over a deep gorge, risking a fall into either pride or despair
C. A steep mountain path, risking a fall into doubt or fanaticism
D. A narrow road at night, risking a fall into unbelief or hypocrisy
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says the right knowledge of God is like working on a razor blade, easy to fall to either extreme: lasciviousness, with no incentive to grow in consecration, or works consciousness.
REF: RIGHTEOUSNESS — [00:15]

Q72. How does the speaker explain why Paul affirmed the Corinthians' standing in Christ in the opening of 1 Corinthians?
A. Paul did not yet know about their problems at the time he wrote the opening lines
B. Paul postponed any discussion of their conduct until he could write a later letter
C. Paul used who they are in Christ by grace as a yardstick to realign unstable believers
D. Paul considered their problems minor compared with the gifts they were exercising
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker contrasts two possibilities, that Paul did not know their problems or that he knew and understood the force of righteousness; he takes the second: Paul used who they are in Christ by grace to realign those who were unstable.
REF: RIGHTEOUSNESS — [01:04; 01:48]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 1 Corinthians 1:4

Q73. Which pairing matches what the speaker says Paul knew about the Corinthians when he affirmed their identity in Christ?
A. Lawsuits among believers, in 1 Corinthians 14
B. Sexual immorality, in 1 Corinthians 5
C. Misuse of spiritual gifts, in 1 Corinthians 6
D. Disorder at the Lord's table, in 1 Corinthians 5
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker lists what Paul knew: sexual immorality (1 Corinthians 5), lawsuits (6), disorder at the Lord's table (11), and misuse of gifts (14), and yet he still emphasized their identity in Christ.
REF: RIGHTEOUSNESS — [02:47]

Q74. Why does the speaker say Paul and the other apostles called it "repentance towards God"?
A. Repentance is mainly an awareness of guilt over the past, which then moves a person to change course
B. Repentance is measured by how fully and how quickly a person's conduct has changed
C. Repentance is directed to God alone and never involves the people one has wronged
D. There must be something a person shifts to, not just from, because repentance responds to light
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker says there must be something you are shifting to, not just something you are shifting from, and not just guilt: repentance is a response to light.
REF: RIGHTEOUSNESS — [03:34]

Q75. How does the speaker interpret Ephesians 1's statement that believers are chosen to be "holy and without blame"?
A. They are a status in Christ by grace, settled before people did anything right or wrong
B. They are a standard that believers must eventually reach through growth in consecration
C. They are a reward that God gives after a believer's repentance has been completed
D. They are an ideal that applies fully only to believers after they have died
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: Reading Ephesians 1:3-6, the speaker says holiness and blamelessness are a status in Christ by grace, determined before we did right or wrong, with righteousness reckoned by faith in Jesus.
REF: RIGHTEOUSNESS — [04:26]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Ephesians 1:3–6

Q76. How does the speaker define righteousness?
A. A record of conduct that God finds acceptable over a lifetime of obedience
B. The inner discipline that lets a believer resist sin consistently over time
C. The absence of any sin in a believer's life after the moment of conversion
D. Standing before God as full beneficiaries of all that Christ has done, by grace
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker defines righteousness as standing before God as full beneficiaries of all that Christ has done, so that by grace believers are worthy of Christ's love and of a relationship with God forever.
REF: RIGHTEOUSNESS — [05:11]

Q77. When a believer sins, how does the speaker say they should approach God in prayer?
A. After first assessing their own behavior to be sure that they qualify to pray
B. By faith in Christ their advocate, not by first assessing how well they have behaved
C. Only after they have fully stopped the sin and shown that the change is lasting
D. Only by asking for forgiveness and for nothing else until the sin is dealt with
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says it is not that every time we pray we first assess how well we have behaved; we have an advocate with the Father, and faith in what Christ has done gives access, while right standing comes from faith alone, not behavior.
REF: RIGHTEOUSNESS — [06:12; 06:53]

Q78. In the church drama the speaker describes, what happens just as the accused sinner is about to be condemned?
A. An angel steps forward and reads out the sinner's good deeds in his defense
B. The judge delays the sentence to give the sinner time to repent first
C. Jesus appears and says, in effect, "see my blood, I died for him"
D. The sinner pleads for mercy and the judge agrees to a lighter sentence
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker recalls a court-setting drama in which, just as the sinner was about to be condemned, Jesus came out and said in effect, see my blood, I died for him.
REF: JUSTIFICATION — [00:00]

Q79. What does the lesson say the Greek word often used for "justify" means?
A. To make morally perfect over time
B. To declare righteous, acquit or vindicate
C. To empower for holy living
D. To forgive and forget
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson says it means to declare righteous, or to acquit or vindicate. It is like a judge saying "discharged and acquitted."
REF: Justification — 05:03

Q80. Why does the speaker say Jesus' words to the criminal on the cross show "a judge talking"?
A. Because Jesus sentenced the criminal for his crimes
B. Because the criminal had earned paradise by confessing his crimes
C. Because Jesus' declaration that the man would be with him in paradise that day was a verdict of not guilty
D. Because Jesus postponed the criminal's verdict to a later date
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: Jesus said "today you shall be with me in paradise." The speaker says this is a judge declaring the man not guilty.

Q81. What does the speaker take from Abraham's appeal in Genesis 18:25 over Sodom and Gomorrah?
A. Abraham knew God as the judge of the whole earth who does right
B. Abraham regarded God's coming judgment on the cities as unfair
C. Abraham saw God mainly as a merciful father rather than a judge
D. Abraham believed that only the nation of Israel would ever be judged
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says that in asking whether the judge of all the earth shall not do right, Abraham showed he knew God was, among other things, the judge of the whole earth.

Q82. What does the speaker point out about 2 Corinthians 5:10 compared with Romans 14:10-12?
A. It limits appearing before the judgment seat to unbelievers alone
B. It says that Christ will judge only entire nations at the end and never individual people
C. It says that believers will not be called on to give any account
D. It names Christ's judgment seat, where Romans 14 names the judgment seat of God
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker reads Romans 14 (all will stand before the judgment seat of God and give account) and 2 Corinthians 5:10 (all must appear before the judgment seat of Christ), noting that this one says specifically Christ.
REF: JUSTIFICATION — [02:10]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Romans 14:10–12; 2 Corinthians 5:10 | Also cited in lesson segment: Genesis 18:25; 1 Samuel 2:10; Psalm 7:11; Romans 8

Q83. How does the speaker describe the relationship between justification and condemnation, drawing on Romans 8?
A. They are two different names for one and the same verdict from the judge
B. They are opposite legal terms: a person is either justified or condemned
C. They are successive stages of one legal process that ends in acquittal
D. They are unrelated ideas, since one is legal and the other is spiritual
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker first calls them synonyms, then corrects himself to antonyms, opposite words, so a person is either justified or condemned, and both are legal terms.
REF: JUSTIFICATION — [03:11]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Romans 8 | Also cited in lesson segment: Psalm 7:11; Romans 14:10, 12; 2 Corinthians 5:10

Q84. What does the speaker say "no condemnation" in Romans 8:1 means for those in Christ Jesus?
A. They no longer commit any wrongdoing once they have come to be in Christ
B. They are spared every earthly consequence of what they did before believing
C. They can no longer be sentenced for their wrongdoings, since they are in Christ
D. They are still sentenced but the penalty is reduced to a lighter one
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker treats condemnation as legal language, like a court sentencing the accused; so no condemnation means those in Christ can no longer be sentenced for their wrongdoings.
REF: JUSTIFICATION — [04:06; 09:24]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Romans 8:1

Q85. Why does the speaker say that, in evangelism, understanding condemnation is needed to appreciate justification?
A. Fear of condemnation is what produces lasting holiness in the lives of believers
B. Condemnation remains a believer's status until their good works over many years have proved otherwise
C. Justification applies only to people who have already been sentenced by a human court
D. People must see they deserve death, the wages of sin, before eternal life in Christ makes sense
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker says that to appreciate justification you must understand condemnation: you deserve to die, the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
REF: JUSTIFICATION — [05:03]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 6:23; Romans 8:1

Q86. How does the speaker connect John 3:16 to a person being found not guilty?
A. It shows that God acquits people whose faith is greater than the weight of their sin
B. It shows the Father's love in giving his Son, who as substitute died the person's death
C. It shows that God simply overlooks sin because he loves the whole world so much
D. It shows that the Son's death makes forgiveness automatic whether or not a person believes
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says a person is found not guilty on one basis alone, that Christ is his substitute, and calls this the love of the Father in John 3:16: he let his Son die for you.
REF: JUSTIFICATION — [05:03; 06:07]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: John 3:16

Q87. What does the speaker's ledger analogy teach?
A. Wrongdoings are a debt on one side; the blood of Jesus on the other is enough to blot out every one
B. Good deeds on one side can be weighed against wrongdoings on the other to reach a balance
C. God keeps a running record of a person's conduct that is carefully reviewed at the end of life, and weighs it
D. Each separate sin must be answered by its own offering before it can be cleared
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker describes a ledger with all of a person's wrongdoing on one side and the precious blood of Jesus on the other; he says one drop of that blood is sufficient and efficacious to blot out every wrongdoing.
REF: JUSTIFICATION — [06:07; 07:06]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: John 3:16

Q88. How does the speaker characterize justification?
A. An inner change in a person's very nature, like a change of essence
B. A reward that is granted after a believer has lived righteously for a time
C. A legal status that results once the judge declares a person not guilty
D. A feeling of relief that depends on how confident a believer happens to feel
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker says justification is a legal term and a status, not quite an essence; once the judge has declared you not guilty, that has become your status.
REF: JUSTIFICATION — [07:06]
BIBLE: Added from online research: Romans 8:33–34 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Romans+8%3A33%E2%80%9334/)

Q89. Someone keeps reminding a believer of his past and calling him guilty. Which response best reflects the lesson on justification?
A. He should assume his accusers may be right until he proves himself.
B. Once the judge has declared him not guilty, no other opinion holds sway, regardless of where he has been or what he has done.
C. He should defend himself before every accuser.
D. He should wait for his behaviour to confirm the verdict.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says that when the judge declares you not guilty, nobody can call you guilty and no other opinion holds sway.
REF: Justification — 07:06–08:16
BIBLE: Added from online research: Romans 8:33–34 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Romans+8%3A33%E2%80%9334/)

Q90. How does the lesson distinguish redemption from justification?
A. Redemption applies only to Old Testament believers, while justification applies to the church.
B. Redemption is the believer's response, while justification is God's gift.
C. Redemption describes the provision of salvation (Christ dying and rising again), while justification is the legal declaration that the believer is not guilty.
D. They are the same thing described in different words.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: Redemption describes the provision or execution of salvation. Justification is the legal declaration.
REF: Justification — 08:16–09:24

Q91. In the speaker's stolen-car illustration, which element corresponds to justification?
A. The kinsman redeemer going and paying what was owed for the stolen car
B. The clearing of the record: the declaration that the person is henceforth not guilty
C. The person being sent to prison for the theft until the penalty is served
D. The person's sincere promise to the judge that he will never steal anything again
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: In the illustration, paying what is owed corresponds to redemption, the provision of salvation, while the clearing of the record, the declaration that the person is henceforth not guilty, is justification.
REF: JUSTIFICATION — [09:24]
